ISSUE A WRIT IN THE NATURE  OF CERTIORARI THEREBY QUASHING THE IMPUGNED ORDER  DATED 30.04.2015 PASSED BY THE LEARNED SENIOR CIVIL  JUDGE, LINGASUGUR IN E.P.NO.182/2011 ON APPLICATION  -2-  WP No. 206984 of 2015 DATED 09.04.2014 VIDE ANNEXURE-D AS AT ANNEXURE-F TO THE PETITION.
THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR PRELIMINARY HEARING IN 'B' GROUP

, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER 1.

The petitioner is before this Court seeking for the following relief's :
"To issue a writ in the nature of certiorari, thereby quashing the impugned order dated 09.01.2015 passed by the learned Senior Civil Judge, Lingasugur, in LAC No.52/2006 on application dated 26.11.2014 (vide Annexure-A) as at Annexure-C to the petition.

Issue a writ in the nature of certiorari, thereby quashing the impugned order dated 30.04.2015 passed by the learned Senior Civil Judge, Lingasugur in E.P.No.182/2011 on application dated 09.04.2014 (vide Annexure-D) as at Annexure-F to the petition.

2. The petitioner - Special Land Acquisition Officer had filed an application in LAC No.52/2006 seeking for correction of alleged error regarding the awardal of additional market value at the rate of 12% interest from the date of 4(1) notification to the date of award rather than the date of the possession.

The said application came to be dismissed by the Senior Civil Judge at Lingasugur vide its order dated 09.01.2015 on the ground that the award having been challenged by the petitioner in MFA No.4871/2008.
There is no such ground which had been taken up in the said miscellaneous first appeal.

The appeal having been dismissed on 11.11.2019 and the present application having been filed on 26.11.2014, after filing of the execution proceedings, the Trial Court came to a conclusion that the application is bereft of merits filed after lapse of about six years from the date on which the original award had been passed and as such, dismissed the application.

3. The petitioner had also filed an objection to the execution proceedings on similar grounds which came to be dismissed by the impugned order dated 30.04.2015 on the same ground as the earlier application.
It is challenging both the said orders that the present petition has been filed.

4. Sri Chaitanyakumar Chandriki, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner would submit that in terms of Section 23(1A) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, the additional market value could be Special Land Acqusition Officer vs Shrikantha S/O Vittayya M G S/O Ramayya on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51967950/
2 awarded only until the date of the award or the date of taking possession of the land whichever is earlier.

sentences.text: 5. In the present case, the possession having been taken earlier to the date of award, the additional compensation could be granted only until the date of possession whereas the Court had granted compensation until the date of approval of the award.
6. Though the respondent has been served none has entered appearance.

7. Heard Sri Chaitanyakumar Chandriki learned counsel appearing for the petitioner and perused the papers.
8.
The facts are not in dispute inasmuch as Section 4(1) notification was issued on 06.09.2001.
The compensation in LAC No.52/2006 was awarded on 10.04.2007.
The appeal in MFA No.4871/2008 was filed in the year 2008 and came to be dismissed by this Court on 11.11.2009 and it is thereafter applications were filed on 26.11.2014.
Thus, it is clear that from the date of original award passed by the Trial Court on 10.04.2007, there is long lapse of seven years in filing the applications.
It is clear that this particular ground had not been taken-up in the appeal filed challenging the award passed by the Trial Court.
The appeal also having been disposed in the year 2009.
The applications were filed in the year 2014 in the execution proceedings.
9. Firstly, such an application could not have been filed in the execution proceedings for the reason that the execution Court could not go beyond the award which had been passed.

Secondly, there is a delay of almost seven years in seeking for rectification of the award passed by the Trial Court which was filed after the dismissal of the miscellaneous first appeal which has not been challenged thereafter, would in my considered opinion disentitles the petitioner from re-agitating this issue before the trial Court after filing of the execution proceedings.
10. These factors having been taken into consideration by the trial Court, I do not find any infirmity in the orders passed by the Trial Court, as such the petition stands dismissed.
